definitions.meaning: The first place after the decimal point: the whole split into ten equal parts, so each part is one tenth and 0.4 is four tenths.
The second place after the decimal point: the whole split into one hundred tiny parts, so 0.25 is twenty-five hundredths.
What a digit is worth because of where it stands: the same 4 is worth four tenths in 0.4 and would be worth four hundredths in 0.04.
The dot that separates the wholes from the tenths: everything to its right is less than one whole.

mechanismSteps: Tenths: one bar, ten equal parts: split one whole bar into ten equal parts and shade four - that shaded amount is 0.4, four tenths.
Hundredths: one square, one hundred tiny parts: split the whole square into ten rows and ten columns and shade twenty-five tiny parts - 0.20 plus 0.05 is 0.25.
Add: line up the places: write 0.4 as 0.40, line up tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths, then add to get 0.40 + 0.25 = 0.65.
Watch out: 0.25 is not bigger than 0.4: compare the covered amounts, not the digit counts - forty hundredths covers more of the whole than twenty-five hundredths.
objectives: Read decimals by place value in the tenths and hundredths places
Add decimals by matching place values first, writing 0.4 as 0.40
subject: math
title: Decimals: place value and adding 0.4 + 0.25

trap.explanation: Longer digit strings feel larger, but place value decides, not digit count. Match the place values first: 0.4 is 0.40, then tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. In the animation scene s4 the tenths bar and the hundredths square are laid over the same whole, and 0.4 visibly covers more: never judge a decimal by how many digits it has.
trap.misconception: Comparing decimals by digit count: 0.25 looks bigger than 0.4 because 25 > 4.

workedExample: In scene s3, 0.4 + 0.25 is worked by matching the places first: 0.4 is rewritten as 0.40, then forty hundredths plus twenty-five hundredths makes sixty-five hundredths. Step by step: 0.4 = 0.40, then 0.40 + 0.25 = 0.65.
